Asha — thanks for sending the worksheet. We completed the template and attached a short guidance doc and our projection workbook. Highlights below; the completed fields are in jonas-edgescale-projection.xlsx and the short playbook is redwood-dedicated-pod-sizing-guide.pdf (both attached).

Summary (high level):
- Recommended GPU families: H100 for low-latency critical routes (best price/perf for 100B with fp16/4-bit quant), A100 for stable mid-range latency with good throughput, and L4-style instances for cost-efficient smaller-context workloads and embedding pipelines.
- Per-pod throughput (100B, 512 ctx) approximations: H100 ~ 85-110 reqs/s (conservative range), A100 ~ 55-75 reqs/s, L4 ~ 18-30 reqs/s (depends on quantization & batch). We included percentile ranges and assumptions in the workbook.
- Burst capacity model: Redwood Dedicated supports two modes — "reserved+burst" (burst carved from reserved headroom within the committed pool using prioritized fair-share) and "separate-burst-lane" (on-demand nodes outside the commit, metered differently). You can choose either; we recommend reserved+burst for predictable unit economics and separate-burst-lane when you require isolation from commitment usage.
- Cross-region fallback: Automated routing to an EU pool is supported via policy-based routing. Data residency is honored for requests that include region-tagging; fallback will only route requests if the customer policy allows cross-region processing for that workload. For strict residency workloads we configure a failover that returns a 503/queued state rather than cross-region execution.

Operational notes:
- Packing & slotting: We pack workloads by model family and latency class. Smaller models share L4 nodes; large autoregressive models get dedicated slots (1–4 slots per GPU depending on KV cache usage).
- Quantization & kernel fit: using int8/4-bit kernels gives 1.8–3× throughput improvement vs fp16 for some models, but we specify these as options in the workbook per-model.
- Tail latency mitigation: we recommend a small KV-cache warm pool (10–15% capacity) to reduce cold-start tails for chat workloads.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached workbook and tell us which workload classes you want validated in a live throughput run.
2) We suggest a 60–90 minute workshop next week to walk scenarios and align on billing for burst lanes.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pod-sizing-guide.pdf, jonas-edgescale-projection.xlsx

--

Thanks — answers inline and I've updated jonas-edgescale-projection.xlsx and added a CSV with slotting scenarios (slotting-scenarios.csv).

Answers (concise):
- Canonical metric: we provide both "peak steady-state reqs/s (concurrent single-stream workers)" and "tokens/s (batched)". For procurement comparisons use the peak steady-state reqs/s at 95th tail < target latency (we included those columns). Example mapping: H100 100B @512 = ~95 reqs/s (single-stream steady) which maps to ~6.5k tokens/s at a 68-token average response.
- Billing & reporting: reserved+burst shows as single committed line on your invoice with a separate burst metering table. Console exposes per-pool utilization (committed consumption vs burst consumption) and line-item billing export (CSV). We'll include a sample invoice export in the workshop packet.
- SOW residency policy (suggested clause): "Redwood will not route customer-facing chat workloads tagged with 'residency:US' to any non-US data plane. In the event the US pool has no available capacity, Redwood will queue the request and return a 503 with retry guidance unless the customer provides written consent to allow cross-region execution."

Operational caveats: if you want automatic queuing vs returning 503 we can implement a short hold window (30–120s) that attempts to free capacity before failing; this is configurable per-route.

Proposed validation workshop: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:00–12:30 PDT — we'll run two short load tests (chat steady-state + batching embedding pipeline) using your sanitized sample traces. Please confirm attendee list; we'll bring an infra engineer and a billing product manager.

Attachments: slotting-scenarios.csv, (updated) jonas-edgescale-projection.xlsx
